reviews.scope: Interpreting favorable-to-total measure ratios as event probabilities within [0,1]
reviews.reason: Geometric probability requires interpreting measure ratios as event likelihoods and verifying that probabilities lie in [0,1], which is the core probability concept in cnm_285, even though discrete equiprobable counting is not used.

reviews.scope: Solving linear inequalities to determine favorable interval lengths in segment cut models
reviews.reason: The algebraic string-cut method translates segment-length conditions into one-variable linear inequalities on a number line to find favorable interval length, whereas other geometric probability models use direct geometric ratios without inequalities.
reviews.counterexample: Planar region or symmetric segment probability problems can compute favorable-to-total measure ratios directly from geometry without solving linear inequalities.

reviews.scope: Computing favorable-to-total volume ratios for spherical regions in 3D geometric probability
reviews.reason: Uniform 3D geometric probability over concentric or disjoint spheres uses the cubic radius-to-volume scaling from cnm_h112 to compute volume ratios, whereas 1D segment, 2D planar, and polyhedral volume problems do not.
reviews.counterexample: One-dimensional segment, two-dimensional planar area, and non-spherical solid probability models compute measure ratios without sphere volume formulas.

reviews.scope: Selecting unique angles with given sine or cosine values and evaluating compositions
reviews.reason: Defining arcsin(t) and arccos(t) as the unique angles in [-pi/2,pi/2] and [0,pi] with a given sine or cosine and evaluating trigonometric compositions directly requires unit-circle sine and cosine definitions and standard values.

reviews.scope: Restricting domains for invertibility, composition identities, and inverse versus reciprocal notation
reviews.reason: General inverse-function concepts motivate why restricting domains yields one-to-one branches and clarify inverse notation and composition rules, but arcsin and arccos can be applied directly from their principal-angle definitions without affine inverses.
reviews.counterexample: Learners can evaluate arcsin(t), arccos(t), and restricted trigonometric compositions directly from unit-circle angle definitions without solving affine inverse functions f(x)=ax+b.

reviews.scope: Justifying uniqueness and range bounds of the principal inverse-sine branch on [-pi/2,pi/2]
reviews.reason: Knowing that sine is strictly increasing on [-pi/2,pi/2] with endpoint values -1 and 1 explains why each input in [-1,1] has a unique principal arcsin angle, though unit-circle coordinates and arccos tasks bypass it.
reviews.counterexample: Principal angles for arcsin(t) and arccos(t) can be identified directly from unique vertical or horizontal coordinates on the unit half-circle without analyzing sine monotonicity intervals.

reviews.scope: Comparing principal-branch conventions across inverse sine, inverse cosine, and inverse tangent
reviews.reason: Principal inverse sine/cosine and principal inverse tangent are parallel conventions restricting periodic trigonometric functions to one-to-one intervals, but evaluating arcsin and arccos does not depend on tangent definitions or tangent equations.
reviews.counterexample: Evaluating arcsin, arccos, and sine/cosine compositions uses only [-pi/2,pi/2] and [0,pi] angle selection on the unit circle without arctan or tan(x)=t solutions.

reviews.scope: Eliminating inconsistent possible worlds and testing whether propositions hold across remaining candidates
reviews.reason: Static finite constraint deduction introduces eliminating impossible assignments, testing whether a claim holds in all remaining possibilities, and giving counterexamples, which prepares for epistemic world elimination without requiring self-referential truth-count puzzles.
reviews.counterexample: When a public-knowledge problem provides an explicit table of possible worlds, learners can partition by observations and eliminate worlds without solving self-referential truth-count constraints.

reviews.scope: Generating initial finite possible worlds from bounded integer equations in card tasks
reviews.reason: In epistemic puzzles where possible worlds are positive integer tuples satisfying sum or product conditions, solving bounded integer equations generates the initial candidate worlds before applying private observations and public announcements.
reviews.counterexample: Public-announcement puzzles that supply an explicit finite list of candidate worlds or non-numeric attributes do not require solving integer Diophantine equations.

reviews.scope: Enumerating valid finite order or attribute worlds to form private observation classes
reviews.reason: One method for private-observation problems explicitly enumerates all finite order or attribute assignments satisfying the stated constraints to build each observer's equivalence class, whereas symbolic two-world counterexamples can refute knowledge without full enumeration.
reviews.counterexample: Refuting claimed knowledge only requires exhibiting two specific indistinguishable worlds that disagree on the target proposition, bypassing complete enumeration of all constraint-satisfying assignments.
